info.title: Alelyon API
info.description:
Machine-facing surface of the Alelyon platform. Read-only in v1. Successfully covered stored market values are dither-quantized under a persisted capture certificate; endpoints serve coverage evidence next to the data. Fresh market/FRED responses expose only their exact committed capture outcome; fresh failures expose null. Store reads may expose a labeled aggregate history view, which is not itself a response-value commitment. Certificate semantics: aggregate `delta_max`/`error_var_max` span ALL columns of a scope (for bars, Volume dominates) — use the per-column `columns` block for the quantization step Δ; the tight storage-only absolute-error bound is |error| <= Δ/2. A fail-open capture (rare, logged) stores raw values that show up as `uncovered_rows`, never as falsely-certified. Live-engine status is observed through the engine's own published state — this service can never act on the engine.

AUTH — with no API key configured the server runs in OPEN mode and serves loopback clients only; any non-local peer gets 403. Set ALELYON_API_KEY and every request must carry `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Keys are 32-512 visible-ASCII tokens (generate one with `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)`). Open mode also validates Host, a present browser Origin, and present Fetch Metadata; omitted Fetch Metadata is not an authentication boundary. Behind a reverse proxy the peer address is the proxy's, so open mode cannot see through it: if you terminate remotely, SET A KEY.

ERRORS — most non-2xx replies carry a `detail` string; FastAPI request-validation 422 replies carry a structured `detail` array. 400 means malformed HTTP framing; 413 means a request body exceeded 64 KiB. 401 means an invalid or missing key; 403 means open mode refused a non-loopback peer or remote plaintext bearer request; 404 means the scope holds no data; 422 means the request was malformed or could not be expressed; 503 means invalid server auth configuration, an upstream engine, or an unconfigured LLM author is unavailable. A 503 means unavailable, never 'the answer is zero'.

get.description:
Aggregate capture certificate for ('bars', TICKER, interval) or
('series', kind, key). delta_max/error_var_max span ALL columns of the
scope; the `columns` block carries each per-column quantization step Δ and
error variance (for bars, use columns.close; the tight storage-only bound is
|error| <= Δ/2 — Volume dominates the scope-wide number).

delta_max/error_var_max are NULL when no column committed a usable Δ — read
that as "not measured", never as "measured as zero". A Δ of 0.0 is a real and
meaningful value (the capture quantizer emits it only for an all-zero column),
which is exactly why an unknown one must not be rendered as one.

Scope lookup retries the conventional casing (lowercase kind, uppercase key)
so a certified scope never 404s on case.

get.description:
Batched last prices. Successfully covered prices carry the exact
same-call capture certificate; a missing certificate is never replaced with
a stale scope aggregate. Certificates are not attached by default (a batch
would double the payload) — pass include_certs=true for per-symbol current
capture evidence. The separate /v1/system/certificates route reports stored
scope history, not proof for this response.

At most 100 symbols are priced per call; anything beyond that is dropped.
`requested`/`returned`/`truncated` in the reply say whether that happened —
chunk the request rather than trusting a short answer.

The L/S screener board (anchored-VWAP z, RSI, rel-vol) — a LIST of
tiles, one per symbol. An unrecognized `timeframe` falls back to Daily.

parameters.name: symbols

schema.description: Comma-separated market symbols. Empty selects the default board. The selected decoded value is at most 4,096 characters; after surrounding whitespace is trimmed, at most 100 non-empty entries of 1-32 letters, digits, dot, hyphen, equals, or caret and containing at least one letter or digit are admitted. Symbols are uppercased and stable-deduplicated. Repeat parameters and invalid entries return 422 before provider access.

response shape. 503 when no LLM author is configured.

get.description:
The co-signing witness seam's public key. A client that pins this key out of
band can confirm (via `alelyon.verify` with `witness_key_hex`) that it signed the
same complete tree head.

Read the caveat: this reference witness is co-located with the signer (the same
operator holds both keys), so pinning this key demonstrates the wire format but
supplies no operator separation. Equivocation resistance requires a different
party to operate the witness and preserve its retained state; this endpoint is
the seam such an operator replaces.

post.description:
Issue a SIGNED CNE for a DSL program (or a question the LLM turns into one).
When the capture store is readable the per-input deltas are transparency-
anchored to the signed cert_log, so the width becomes third-party-checkable
(see the reply's `envelope.inputs[].transparency` and the verifier's
`width_trust`). Each anchored input also carries a witness co-signature over its
complete STH (see `witness_key_id` + `GET /witness/pubkey`). A client that pins
that witness key out of band can verify the same-head co-signature; independence
exists only when a party other than the signer operates the witness and retains
its state. The reply is portable: verify it with `alelyon.verify` + the pinned
signer key. 422 if the request yields no program; 503 if the LLM author is needed
but unconfigured.
